eden_corp_prod: Hi team — during yesterday's load test we saw our org hit 0 credits around 23:50 local, API returned 429s, UI showed 0 for ~12 minutes, then refilled and calls resumed. Can someone explain why it flashed to zero then came back? We didn't change plan.
lee_support: Sorry you're hitting this, thanks for the report. Can you share the org id and any reproducible steps? Quick guess: burst + retries during a maintenance window can exhaust visible quota while backfills/processes reconcile.
eden_corp_prod: Org: org_9a8b7c. Repro: run 200 concurrent short requests (~50 tokens each) + retry on 429s with 200ms backoff for ~6 minutes. Happens reliably in our staging.
mike_infra: Thanks. I pulled the logs for org_9a8b7c around 4310000001. We saw a burst of requests hitting the edge and our edge cache for quota decisions was overloaded. Central quota store accepted the refill at 00:00 UTC but edge caches still had a stale zero state for ~10m while cache-warm finished.
eden_corp_prod: So the API was returning 429 but backend had credits? Why the 12 minute gap vs the 0:00 reset?
lee_support: Two separate issues layered: 1) Reset timing vs billing anchor — this tenant's billing anchor is aligned to UTC midnight, so central bucket refilled exactly at 00:00 UTC. 2) Edge cache TTL and our maintenance that rotated some quota cache nodes caused slower propagation. During that window the edge served stale quota = 0 even though the central service had the new tokens.
sophie_billing: Adding: for monthly buckets we persist the refill marker in central ledger at the billing boundary. Any in-flight edge-level rate-limiters rely on cached state with a short TTL (default 60s) but under high load we extend or stall invalidation. That explains the "flash zero" behavior.
eden_corp_prod: Is there a recommended mitigation? Our app retries quickly and that seems to amplify the problem.
mike_infra: Yes. Short-term: implement exponential backoff + jitter on 429s and respect Retry-After header. Also set idempotency keys for retried requests to avoid double counting across retries.
lee_support: We can also propose two customer-facing mitigations: 1) Request a higher burst quota or smoothing window so your peak concurrency doesn't touch zero. 2) Consider Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.
eden_corp_prod: Can you share the exact repro steps we should run so we can validate fixes on our side?
lee_support: Repro we used: run 200 concurrent POSTs to /v1/generate with 50 tokens avg, simulate client retry loop: if 429 then wait 200ms then retry (max 5). Run for 6 minutes starting 30s before billing boundary. Observe: API 429 spikes at boundary, UI shows 0 while central ledger shows refill happened.
quota-bot: automated note: account org_9a8b7c hit quota_exhausted at 4310000007, central refill applied at 4310000000, edge cache invalidation completed at 4310000600.
eden_corp_prod: Ok that matches our runs. Anything Redwood can change so this doesn't recur for others?
mike_infra: We're adding a safeguard: if central ledger indicates a fresh refill, edges will accept a short-window grace period to avoid returning 429 immediately while cache invalidates. It's a config roll that should reduce these 0->refill flashes. ETA: canary in next 48h.
lee_support: I'll open a support ticket to track SUS-1829 and keep you updated. As a short-term action I changed org_9a8b7c's burst window + raised retry headers so your clients get Retry-After: 5s during the flip.
sophie_billing: Also verified there's no billing/proration on the account for that month — no unexpected depletion.
eden_corp_prod: Thanks, appreciate the quick follow-up. Will implement exponential backoff and we can re-run the loadtest after the canary. :thumbsup:
lee_support: Sounds good — ping here once you re-run and we'll correlate logs. :eyes:
